冠 means a crown or ceremonial head covering, and can also express being foremost or peerless. 冠 (かんむり) names the headgear; 王冠 (おうかん) is a royal crown and also a crown-type bottle cap. Learn each complete word rather than translating every 冠 compound as a physical crown.

Modern-shape mnemonic: imagine the cover-like 冖 as a crown over 元, with 寸 at the lower right to hold it in place. This is an invented memory aid, not a historical explanation or a verified phonetic analysis.
Both complete source readings are selected for practice. The native noun かんむり and the compound reading カン have separate examples.

The "peerless" meaning belongs to the reading かん, not the native noun かんむり. Recognize the formal expression 世界に冠たる (せかいにかんたる), "foremost in the world," used before a noun.

In kanji terminology, かんむり names a top component: 宀 is called うかんむり. 冠 itself has 冖, without the upper dot of 宀 in 完 and 守. 冗 shares the cover-like top but has a much simpler lower part; 完 contains 元 below its roof, while 守 contains 寸. These are shape comparisons, not claims of a shared origin.

冠 かんむり — crown; ceremonial cap; also a top component of a kanji
冠, read かんむり here, names a crown or diadem, and also traditional ceremonial headgear worn by courtiers or Shinto clergy. It does not mean every everyday hat.
王様は金の冠をかぶっていました。 (おうさまはきんのかんむりをかぶっていました。) - The king was wearing a gold crown.
In kanji terminology, かんむり is a component at the top of a character. For example, 宀 is called うかんむり; this use is not a physical item of clothing.

This is one kanji with the native reading かんむり. Learn the whole pronunciation rather than dividing it into separate sound values. The same written character also has other readings with different uses.
帽子 (ぼうし) is the broader everyday hat or cap word. 冠 can also refer to a name or title attached to a program or event, including named sponsorship; 名前 (なまえ) is not restricted to that use.

The source list's English "first; best" belongs to the separate reading かん, not かんむり. Recognize 冠たる (かんたる), "foremost; peerless," as in 世界に冠たる技術 (せかいにかんたるぎじゅつ), "world-leading technology." This is supplementary reading-specific teaching, not a new meaning pronounced かんむり.

王冠 おうかん — royal crown; crown-type bottle cap

王冠 is a royal crown, worn as a sign of royal status. It can also name a crown awarded as an honor. A separate everyday-object sense is a crown-shaped metal bottle cap, such as the closure on a beer bottle.
王は王冠をかぶっています。 (おうはおうかんをかぶっています。) — The king is wearing a crown.
瓶の王冠を外しました。 (びんのおうかんをはずしました。) — I removed the bottle's crown cap.
The second sentence concerns a bottle closure, not royal headgear. Use the context to choose the English meaning.

王 means "king; ruler," and 冠 means "crown." This is a modifier + head compound: a ruler's crown. The on readings are オウ + カン. The bottle-cap sense extends the name to an object shaped like a crown; it is not a miniature item of royal clothing.

冠 (かんむり) is the broader crown or ceremonial-headgear word. 帽子 (ぼうし) means a hat or cap, not specifically a royal crown. For containers, 蓋 (ふた) is a broader lid or cap word, while 栓 (せん) can mean a stopper or plug. These words overlap for some closures, but are not interchangeable for every object. There is no useful single opposite noun.

王冠 does not name every lid or screw cap: the bottle sense concerns the crown-type metal closure. For the royal object, use かぶる for putting it on and かぶっている for wearing it. Do not transfer the separate 冠たる (かんたる), "peerless," use of 冠 to 王冠.
